subject: RetailEdge: increased 5xx/429 after quant profile v2 rollout — immediate actions
messages:
From: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@retailedge.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2027-02-28T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: sudden spike in 5xx/429s after this morning's update

Hi team,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx and 429 responses at ~07:40 PT after you deployed the 'model-v2-quant-a' change. The storefront started timing out (500) and our checkout API returned 429 on retry. Attached are a small sample of failed requests and timestamps. This is affecting user checkout and we are seeing a 3% revenue loss on the traffic slice going to your API.

Can you confirm whether this rollout touched our Dedicated pool? We kicked off rate limiting on our side to reduce retries but issue persists. Please advise immediate mitigation steps — we need either a rollback or a traffic split to previous model.

Thanks,
Sandra Lopez
CTO, RetailEdge
Sent from my iPhone
From: support@redwood-inference.com <support@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@retailedge.com>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 5xx/429s after this morning's update

Sandra —

Thanks for the samples. We see correlated error spikes and elevated latency in our ingest pipeline for your account (RetailEdge). I've opened an internal escalation and looped in the on-call engineering lead. Short-term: we've temporarily limited concurrent long-polling requests from your edge to reduce retry cascades while we investigate.

We will follow up with a plan within 30 minutes.

— Redwood Support
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@retailedge.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: RetailEdge — urgent: suspected quant profile rollback request

Karthik / Rishi,

RetailEdge is reporting a sharp increase in 5xx/429 and timeouts after this morning's rollout of model-v2-quant-a. Symptoms: elevated per-token latency (p95 jumped ~600ms), 429s concentrated on short-sequence requests, and retry storms from their edge leading to cascading 500s. Samples attached.

Observability notes:
- A subset of our Dedicated GPU pods serving RetailEdge received the quantized kernel update at 07:30 PT (canary -> full for their pool).
- Telemetry shows increased kernel-level memory churn and many KV-cache misses for the quantized path.
- Error codes are primarily 5xx (502/503) and 429 from our rate limiter because requests are queuing up.

Immediate ask: can we roll Traffic for RetailEdge back to model-v1-quant-stable and pin them there while we debug? If rollback is not safe, we need a quick guard (route to host-model non-quant variant or apply a kernel fallback).

Please confirm actions and ETA. I'm also putting Marissa (CS lead) on the thread to coordinate communication and credits if needed. Sandra — apologies, we're treating this as P1.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@retailedge.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RetailEdge — urgent: suspected quant profile rollback request

Olga / team —

Quick diagnostic: the rollout triggered activation of the "int8-dynamic-kernel" path for this model family on a subset of the Dedicated fleet. For most workloads this path reduces token compute, but in retail queries we've seen KV cache fragmentation and repeated cache rehydration on short sequences (title/sku lookups). The fragmentation increases per-request cost and latency, causing queueing and then 429s when the token budget is consumed.

Action plan (immediate):
1) Roll back RetailEdge traffic to model-v1-quant-stable (pinned) — ETA 10 minutes.
2) Re-deploy the host-model non-quant variant as a failover for their highest-volume routes — ETA 25 minutes.
3) Collect a 2-hour kernel-level trace and a sample of failing requests; share with infra for root-cause.

I'll start the rollback now and post updates. If rollback fails, we'll take the Dedicated pool out of rotation and rehydrate from a cold host variant (temporary capacity hit).

Karthik
Sr. SRE — Serving Runtime
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@retailedge.com>, marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RetailEdge — urgent: suspected quant profile rollback request

Sandra — quick update: Karthik is rolling your traffic back to the previous quant-stable variant now; we expect the rollback to complete by ~09:25 PT. We will monitor your SLO dashboard and keep you posted on recovery. We will also offer a one-week service credit for the impacted slice while we complete a deeper RCA.

Marissa — please prepare the customer comms (plain-language summary + timeline + credit confirmation).

Olga
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@retailedge.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T12:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RetailEdge — urgent: suspected quant profile rollback request

Final update: rollback completed at 11:05 PT; RetailEdge traffic fully pinned to model-v1-quant-stable. 5xx/429 rates returned to baseline within ~30 minutes after rollback. Root cause (preliminary): an untested quantized kernel variant (int8-dynamic-kernel) enabled a code-path that does aggressive cache compaction on small-sequence workloads; this unexpectedly increased latency for high-QPS short calls and caused request queueing + rate-limiter tripping.

Next steps:
- Infra will revert the canary promotion for int8-dynamic-kernel for the 1-week canary window and add a negative test case for short-sequence KV behavior (owner: rishi).
- We will create a model rollout checklist update that requires short-sequence synthetic traffic gating for quant kernel promotions (owner: Karthik).
- CS: draft customer letter & confirm credit details (owner: Marissa).

Attachments: consolidated error samples and SLO ping traces are in the shared Drive link.

Karthik
